questions.question_text: Find the positive integer $n$ such that $^{n}C_{2} + {^{n}C_{3}} = {^{12}C_{3}}$.

options.why: Equated $n$ to $12$ without accounting for the upper index increasing by $1$.
Added $1$ to $12$ instead of solving $n+1=12$.
Subtracted the lower index $3$ from $12$ instead of subtracting $1$.
Used equal lower indices but omitted the complementary index $13-5=8$.
Subtracted $1$ from both answers even though the combined lower index is $r$.
Used $12-5=7$ for symmetry instead of the combined upper index $13$.

questions.solution_text:
By Pascal's identity:
$^{12}C_{r} + {^{12}C_{r-1}} = {^{13}C_{r}}$
$r = 5$ or $r = 13-5 = 8$.
Both satisfy $1 \le r \le 12$.

questions.question_text: If $^{13}C_{n} = {^{13}C_{4}}$ and $n \ne 4$, find the value of $n$.

options.why: Used the equal lower index despite the condition $n \ne 4$.
Added $13+4$ instead of subtracting $13-4$.
Subtracted an extra $1$, calculating $13-4-1$.

questions.solution_text:
The lower indices are distinct, so they sum to $13$:
$n + 4 = 13$
$n = 9$.

The distinct lower indices sum to the upper index:
$5 + (n+9) = 3n$

questions.question_text: If $^{20}C_{2x+1} + {^{20}C_{2x}} = {^{21}C_{9}}$, find the values of $x$ for which the lower indices are valid integers.

options.why: Solved $2x+1=9$ but omitted the complementary lower index $21-9=12$.
Used $2x$ as the combined lower index instead of $2x+1$.
Used $20-9=11$ for the complementary index instead of $21-9=12$.

questions.solution_text:
By Pascal's identity:
$^{20}C_{2x+1} + {^{20}C_{2x}} = {^{21}C_{2x+1}}$
$2x+1 = 9$ or $2x+1 = 21-9 = 12$.
$x = 4$ or $x = \dfrac{11}{2}$.
The lower indices on the left are $9,8$ or $12,11$, so both answers are valid.
